conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, thanks. I’ve had diarrhea and right lower belly pain for a few days. My ostomy’s been very active—loose and non-bloody. The pain’s not too bad now, but it was worse earlier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any fever, nausea, or vomiting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever or vomiting. I feel tired, but not sick like that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I see you were at the hematology clinic today for your IVIG and they sent you here because of the pain and diarrhea. They gave you two antibiotics—cefepime and flagyl—just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they were worried it might be an infection or something related to my lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s understandable. We’ve reviewed your CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis. It didn’t show any infection, appendicitis, or bowel issue. Everything looks stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s good. So it’s not my lymphoma coming back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No signs of recurrence on the scan. Your lymph nodes and spleen are the same size as before. We also did a chest CT, and those nodules and nodes are stable too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. But why the pain and diarrhea then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Most likely a viral gastroenteritis. Several family members had similar symptoms, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, my sister and nephew had diarrhea last week. They’re better now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That supports the idea of a virus. Your stool tests came back negative for C. diff, Salmonella, Shigella, and Campylobacter.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no bacteria. But what about the blood work? I saw my counts were low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you have pancytopenia—low white blood cells, hemoglobin, and platelets. This has been happening over time. It could be due to viral suppression of your bone marrow, not necessarily lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Could it be my immune deficiency affecting this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: CVID may play a role, but we think the virus is the main trigger right now. We’ll monitor your counts after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my sodium? I saw it dropped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your sodium is now 131. It was 140 on admission. This is likely from the IV fluids you got. You’re not showing symptoms, so we’ll watch it and recheck as an outpatient.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. I’m glad it’s not serious. Do I need more antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No. You only needed that one dose since we don’t think it’s a bacterial infection. We’ll hold off on more.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. The pain is much less, and my ostomy output has slowed down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your labs this morning show your white count and hemoglobin are still low, but we expected that. No new concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the stool virus test?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Came back negative—no virus isolated. But that doesn’t rule out a viral cause. Sometimes tests miss it, especially if you’re already recovering.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. What about the CMV test?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: CMV was not detected. That’s good news. We also checked EBV, HHV6, and parvovirus—results pending, but we’ll follow up at your clinic visit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my iron? I remember my ferritin was low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your ferritin was very low at 10. You received an iron infusion yesterday—ferric gluconate. We’ll recheck your iron studies as an outpatient.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ve been worried about everything at once—lymphoma, counts, infections.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But right now, everything points to a viral illness causing temporary issues. Your lymphoma remains in remission.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. We’re planning to discharge you today. You’re doing well—pain is minimal, output is back to baseline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do after I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue all your regular medications. You have a follow-up in the hematology clinic in two days to check your blood counts and review all the test results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will they check my sodium and iron again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ll repeat your CBC, basic metabolic panel, and iron studies. Also, they’ll follow up on the viral tests—EBV, CMV, etc.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if my counts don’t improve?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If they stay low, we may need to investigate further, but for now, we expect them to recover as you get over this illness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I feel much better knowing it’s not my cancer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. You responded well, and we’re confident this was a viral issue. Just keep an eye on your symptoms and call if you develop fever, severe pain, or increased diarrhea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks for explaining everything so clearly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get your discharge papers ready, and you should be home soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—should I restart my IVIG?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your next Hizentra dose is scheduled for next week. Continue as prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I feel ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad to hear that. Take care, and see you in clinic soon.
